_meta.note: Daytona HackSprint demo cache. Market figures are updated through the July 24, 2026 close; operating figures use Tesla's Q2 2026 shareholder update and 10-Q.
_meta.sources: Tesla Investor Relations Q2 2026 update and Form 10-Q; Nasdaq/StockAnalysis; Yahoo Finance; ADVFN (accessed 2026-07-24)

market_snapshot.price_note: 2026-07-24 regular-session close; -2.08% on the day after the 2026-07-23 post-earnings selloff

why_it_fell_context.trigger: The July 24 decline extended the post-earnings selloff. Tesla's July 22 Q2 report showed adjusted EPS of $0.33 versus roughly $0.50-$0.54 expected, while quarterly free cash flow turned negative as AI, robotics and manufacturing capex accelerated.
why_it_fell_context.but_also_true: Q2 revenue was $28.236B, +25.5% YoY, and Q2 deliveries reached a record 480,126, +25% YoY. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.32 and adjusted EPS was $0.33.
structural_worries: BYD remained the global EV volume leader; Tesla's competitive position depends increasingly on autonomy, energy and robotics
Operating margin fell to 1.4% from 4.1% a year earlier as operating expenses and AI investment increased
Robotaxi and Optimus require heavy spending today while their long-term revenue remains uncertain
Tesla expects 2026 capital expenditures above $25B, driven by AI compute, data centers, manufacturing and company-operated AI-enabled assets
why_it_fell_context.parent_translation_plain: Tesla delivered more cars than ever and revenue grew strongly, but profit per share missed expectations and heavy investment pushed quarterly free cash flow below zero. The stock fell 14.52% on July 23 and another 2.08% on July 24: $10,000 held through both sessions would have become about $8,375.
